# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Term:** 12 months, renewable
**Fee:** US$10,000 per month

## 1. Situation Summary

Dana Whitfield, this proposal draws only on the Client Profile Block prepared from the discovery call notes of 6 October 2026. Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Profile Block records about 1,100 staff and revenue "in the US$200 to 300 million range", which is noted as spoken rather than taken from filings.

The Profile Block lists three AI use cases:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

AI maturity is recorded as Piloting. The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The certification target is ISO/IEC 42001, with work to start next year. That start date is not fixed.

The Profile Block also records:

* **Risk event:** an internal audit finding of June 2026 stating that there is no inventory of AI systems.
* **Incumbent frameworks:** an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function.

The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so there are no carried-forward open items.

Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at Piloting Maturity

At Piloting maturity, governance decisions arrive alongside delivery decisions rather than ahead of them. A pilot moving toward production, a deployed system and a planned system each call for different governance treatment. ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work then adds a management system layer over all three.

A one-time assessment would describe a single moment. A fractional advisor stays engaged as the visual inspection pilot approaches its stated production window, as ISO/IEC 42001 work begins and as sales forecasting moves from plan to design.

The program applies three principles throughout: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. In practice:

* Governance gates are set before production rather than after.
* Each AI decision is recorded with its intended purpose and accepted risk.
* Accountability for outcomes stays with named people at the Client.

The advisor recommends. The Client decides.

## 3. The Annual Arc

The program start date is Unknown and is to be confirmed at intake. The arc below is expressed in program quarters. Because your stated objective points to Q2 2027, the work tied to visual inspection is placed in the first two quarters. If the confirmed start date leaves too little time before Q2 2027, the sequence will be compressed or reordered at intake.

The ISO/IEC 42001 audit date is Unknown, so audit preparation intensity is placed in the third and fourth quarters. It will be re-sequenced once a date is known.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize.** The program will:

* Design and populate an AI system inventory, responding to the June 2026 internal audit finding.
* Map governance roles and decision rights for the three listed use cases.
* Define the governance requirements a pre-production gate for visual inspection would need to satisfy.
* Log EU AI Act and GDPR questions for verification by external counsel. These include how each use case may be classified and when obligations may apply.

The working sessions will use the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) as the structuring framework.

**Quarter 2: Deepen.** The program will help the Client build and run the pre-production governance gate for visual inspection. This covers risk assessment, human oversight design, data handling and decision records.

The program will also review the deployed customer service chatbot against the same governance criteria. The Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) will guide pacing and deliberate decision points so that production readiness is reached through recorded decisions rather than schedule pressure.

**Quarter 3: Assure.** ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work begins in earnest. The program will:

* Run a gap review against the standard's requirements.
* Design evidence collection.
* Hold a readiness review structured for the internal auditor audience listed in the Profile Block.

The output is a readiness view. It is not a prediction of any certification or audit outcome.

**Quarter 4: Evolve.** The program will:

* Bring the planned sales forecasting use case into the governance process at design stage.
* Prepare executive and board-level reporting using AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).
* Update ISO/IEC 42001 readiness status.
* Prepare the year-end review that informs the renewal decision.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

**Monthly executive advisory session.** Covers decisions, risks watched and regulatory developments flagged for counsel verification.

**Monthly working session.** Held with the governance team on the current quarter's artifacts. Who attends each session is Unknown and is to be confirmed at intake. The Profile Block lists these audience roles: General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors.

**Asynchronous availability.** Covers defined question categories, with response windows and escalation paths agreed at intake.

**Quarterly governance review.** Measures progress against the annual arc.

## 5. Scope and Out of Scope

**In scope:**

* Governance evolution
* Implementation guidance
* Audit preparation
* AI strategy
* Executive decision support

**Out of scope:**

* Legal advice
* Certification body functions
* Staff augmentation
* Incident command

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act and GDPR interpretation, route to external counsel. Regulatory developments raised in the program are flagged for verification and are not offered as settled advice.

## 6. Questions to Confirm at Intake

1. What is the program start date, and does the time remaining before Q2 2027 support the sequencing above?
2. What is the planned ISO/IEC 42001 start date, and is there a target audit date? (Currently Unknown.)
3. Does the visual inspection pilot fall within the constraint that the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff? If so, how should consultation timing be reflected in the arc?
4. Does the customer service chatbot process customer data? If so, how does the constraint that customer data must stay in the EU apply to it?
5. Can the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and ISO 9001 quality management system listed in the Profile Block host AI governance elements, and if so, which ones?
6. Who holds decision rights for each listed AI use case? (Currently Unknown.)
7. How does the twelve-month fee align with fiscal years? The Profile Block records budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. Fiscal year dates are Unknown.

## 7. Investment

The fee is US$10,000 per month for 12 months, which is US$120,000 over the full term. The program is renewable. Question 7 above addresses the relationship between this fee and the approved budget recorded in the Profile Block.
